column1: IoT: Threshold Alert Rules per Node
column30:
As a conservation officer, I want an alert raised automatically when a sensor reading breaks a rule, so the team can respond quickly to possible poaching or habitat disturbance.

*Split on 13 Oct 2026.* The rest is now separate stories: CTIP-76 node-silent alert, CTIP-77 notifications, CTIP-78 acknowledge and resolve.

*6 Nov 2026:* alerts are rule-based only. The statistical anomaly model (CTIP-75) was dropped; the AI innovation is now plant identification from a photo (CTIP-141 to CTIP-143).

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] Threshold rules configurable per node: motion, distance change ({{thresholds.distance_change_cm}}), sudden temperature or humidity change, soil drying out
* [ ] A rule breach creates an alert with node, specimen, reading, severity and the captured image if available
* [ ] Rules run in the API when telemetry arrives

column1: IoT: Sensor Node Registration & Alert Routing
column30:
As a system administrator, I want to register sensor nodes and decide who receives their alerts, so each node is tied to the specimen it protects and the right officers are notified.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Admin can register, edit and deactivate a sensor node (ID, location, linked specimen)
* Registering a node issues its own MQTT credentials; deactivating revokes them
* Node GPS position is tracked, and a node moving outside its expected area is flagged
* Admin can set which officers receive alerts per node or per severity
* Only the System Administrator role can access these screens and endpoints

Design and build an improvement to the field ground-truthing workflow that makes plant identification, location, recording or management faster, more accurate or more scalable in remote forest conditions. Automated species identification from photos is out of scope (NeuonAI's product).

*Acceptance criteria*

* Limitations of the current ground-truthing workflow identified and written up
* Improved workflow or design proposed and agreed with the team
* Improvement implemented in the app
* Effectiveness evaluated with a suitable test (for example, time per record before vs after)

*Scope Focus Area 1 — Smart Digital Ground-Truthing Platform* (Objective 1)

Android mobile app ({{apps/mobile}}, Expo) that lets botanists document plant specimens in the field at Niah National Park.

*Connectivity (lecturer directive, 28 Sep 2026):* built online-first, assuming internet is available in the field, so the whole system works end to end first. Full offline data collection and sync are added at the end of Sprint 2 (CTIP-44, CTIP-16). This differs from the submitted proposal, which stated offline-first as a hard requirement.

*Botanist role must be able to:*

* Register new plant records on site
* Record detailed plant information (taxonomy, morphological characteristics, height, related attributes)
* Capture and attach photographs
* Record GPS location
* Synchronise field data with the central database
* Generate / bind a QR code for each plant record so users can view its details

*Also in scope:* QR scanning of tagged plants, searchable plant species reference, offline data collection (Sprint 2, last).

*Stories:* CTIP-15, CTIP-42 (stream A, Sprint 1); CTIP-26, CTIP-27 (stream B, Sprint 1); CTIP-45, CTIP-51 (stream A, Sprint 2); CTIP-44, CTIP-16 (stream B, Sprint 2).

*Outcome:* botanists and conservation officers identify, document and manage plant records during field surveys with less manual effort and better data quality.

*Scope Focus Area 2 — Digital Plant Knowledge System* (Objective 2)

Web-based biodiversity knowledge system ({{apps/web}}, React + Vite) for managing and accessing plant species information.

*Features:* plant taxonomy and scientific names, species descriptions, botanical photographs, conservation status, species distribution maps, search and filtering by scientific or common name.

*Conservation Officer role must be able to:*

* Add, edit and delete plant species records
* Upload plant photographs and supporting information
* Review and approve submitted observations (from the mobile app)
* Search and filter biodiversity records
* Generate and export biodiversity reports

*Outcome:* conservation officers can manage, retrieve and update accurate biodiversity information to support conservation, research and public education.

*Scope Focus Area 3 — Cybersecurity and Data Protection* (Objective 3)

*Implementation (all platforms):*

* Secure login for all users with simple authentication methods
* Encryption of sensitive/personal data
* Role-based access control (Botanist, Conservation Officer, System Administrator, unauthenticated Visitor)

*Application Security Aspect (assessed deliverables):*

* Project planning and execution based on the Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC)
* Vulnerability assessment test plan — tools and scope of testing defined
* Vulnerability assessment results with verification of each vulnerability
* Recommendations and their implementation
* Evidence of reassessment showing the vulnerabilities were fixed

*Team rule:* security implementation and security testing must be done by different people.

*Scope Focus Area 4 — IoT-Enabled Plant Protection* (Objective 4)

GPS and environmental sensor nodes (ESP32-CAM, {{apps/firmware}}) deployed near rare or endangered plant species.

*Basic functionalities:*

* Real-time environmental sensing (temperature, humidity, movement)
* GPS-based plant and sensor tracking
* Threat detection and automated alerts for unusual activity (e.g. potential poaching, habitat disturbance)
* Centralised monitoring dashboard for administrators
* Ecological data storage and analysis

*Out of scope:* production hardware (weatherproofing, solar, LoRa backhaul) and deep learning on sensor time series — threshold rules plus a lightweight statistical model only.

*Outcome:* continuous monitoring of endangered species, rapid response to threats, and long-term habitat records.

column1: Innovation: Spike – Plant Identification Accuracy on Our Species
column30:
As the team, we want to know how well an existing plant-ID service or vision model matches photos to the species in our database, so we can decide by *Wed 11 Nov* whether to build the identification feature.

AI innovation for the Final Stretch Sprint (decided 6 Nov): a botanist points the phone camera at a plant and the app suggests which species in our database it matches. Replaces the AI anomaly model (CTIP-75 dropped; IoT alerts are rule-based only). Relates to CTIP-51. Work on Mon 9 Nov.

*Approach to try first:* an existing plant-ID service or vision model, called from the API (no training data, GPU or model hosting on Render). *Alternative:* image similarity against each species' gallery photos (needs {{GET /species/:id/media}}). Training our own classifier is out of scope.

*Acceptance criteria*

* About 20 photos of species already in our database are tested, ideally real phone photos and not only clean gallery shots
* At least 2 photos of plants not in our database are tested, to see whether "no match" is returned
* The service's free-tier limits, price and terms (including what it does with uploaded images) are written in this ticket
* Results recorded per photo: expected species, top 3 returned, confidence, and whether the match to our species table worked by scientific name (note any synonym problems)
* Ends with a go or no-go and the confidence threshold for "no match"
* Proposed pass mark, to confirm with the team: the right species is in the top 3 for at least 14 of 20 photos
* If no-go: says what the demo and report show instead (rule-based alerts, plus the camera feature as a prototype with these measured results)
* No API key or secret committed (the repository is public)

*Done when* the findings are posted here and in the team chat, and the sprint doc is updated with the decision.

column1: Innovation: POST /species/identify – Match a Photo to Our Species
column30:
As a botanist, I want to send a photo of a plant and get the closest species from our database, so I can classify what I am looking at faster.

*Blocked by CTIP-141* (spike go decision, Wed 11 Nov). Build only if the spike passes. Contract change in {{packages/api-contract/}}: needs a second person's review. Relates to CTIP-51.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] {{POST /species/identify}} takes raw JPEG bytes. Not JPEG answers 415, empty body 422, over 2 MB 413
* [ ] Metadata is removed before the image is sent to any outside service, including EXIF GPS coordinates (threat model: no coordinates leak)
* [ ] Only signed-in staff roles set in {{permissions.js}} can call it. No sign-in answers 401, a role without permission answers 403
* [ ] Rate limited per user. Going over the limit answers 429
* [ ] The result maps to our species table by scientific name, with spelling and synonym differences normalised
* [ ] Answers with up to 3 matches, each with species id, name and confidence, or {{no match}} when the best confidence is under the threshold agreed in CTIP-141
* [ ] A result not in our database is reported as "not in our database" and is never returned as a species record
* [ ] If the outside service fails or times out, the API answers a clear error (502 or 504) without leaking the provider's error text or key
* [ ] The third-party key is read from Render's environment variables only, and is not in the repository, the logs or the APK
* [ ] The image is not stored, unless a later story adds saving it to a species record
* [ ] Route added to {{permissions.js}} and {{packages/api-contract/}}, with a second person's review
* [ ] {{node --test}} covers: mapping and synonym handling, the threshold, the three image error cases and the provider failure case, using fixed sample responses
* [ ] Merged to {{main}} with {{npm run api:test}} passing
* [ ] Added to the CTIP-74 reassessment checklist

column1: Innovation: Mobile Camera Screen – Identify a Plant from a Photo
column30:
As a botanist in the field, I want to point my phone camera at a plant and see which species in our database it most likely is, so I can classify it and open its record.

*Blocked by CTIP-142* ({{POST /species/identify}}; can start once its contract change is reviewed). Build only if the CTIP-141 spike passes. Relates to CTIP-51.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] A screen in the mobile app opens the camera, or lets the botanist choose an existing photo
* [ ] The photo is sent through the shared API client to {{POST /species/identify}}, with a loading state while waiting
* [ ] Up to 3 matches shown with name and confidence. Tapping one opens that species page
* [ ] A "no match" state when the API says so, with a suggestion to retake the photo from another angle
* [ ] Shown as a suggestion the botanist confirms. The app never changes a record by itself
* [ ] Clear error states: no internet ("Identification needs an internet connection"), rate limited, camera permission denied, server error
* [ ] The photo is not saved to the device gallery or to a record unless the botanist chooses to
* [ ] Works on the demo phones with the final APK
* [ ] Merged to {{main}} with {{npm run lint}} passing, and tried on a real phone with at least 5 species
